answer: Yes. Workday reports a "Gross Revenue Retention Rate" (a gross retention metric; it does not disclose a net revenue retention rate). For FY2025 (as of January 31, 2025), this rate was approximately 98%. Definition: it measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers, calculated by taking total Annual Recurring Revenue ("ARR") of customers as of the corresponding prior period-end and comparing it to ARR from that same set of customers as of the current period-end. The metric reflects recurring revenue lost to product or customer churn, but excludes additional revenue from add-ons or net expansions (volume/price adjustments). ARR itself represents the annualized value of active subscription contracts as of period end (each contract's total contract value divided by contract term in days, multiplied by 365), calculated on a constant-currency basis, and is a non-GAAP measure not meant to substitute for revenue or unearned revenue.
provenance: WDAY FY2025 10-K, MD&A section "Gross Revenue Retention Rate" (text located near offset ~184500–186100 of the filing's primary document).

answer: As of December 31, 2024, Shift4 discloses a vendor concentration risk in that all of its merchant processing activity in North America is facilitated by a single (one) vendor. The company states it believes this vendor maintains appropriate backup systems and alternative arrangements to avoid significant disruption in the event of an unforeseen event. Additionally, because Shift4 is not a "member bank" in North America, it depends on a sponsorship agreement with a single member bank to process bank card transactions; if that agreement is breached, the bank sponsor may terminate it, giving Shift4 180 days to find an alternative bank sponsor.

answer: Yes — Workday reports only a **Gross Revenue Retention Rate** (no net revenue retention metric is disclosed). For fiscal year 2025 (as of January 31, 2025), the gross revenue retention rate was approximately 98%. Definition (per the 10-K, MD&A "Gross Revenue Retention Rate" section): it "measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers" and "is calculated by taking total annual recurring revenue ("ARR") of our customers as of the corresponding prior period-end and comparing that to ARR from that same set of customers as of the current period-end." It accounts for recurring revenue lost to product or customer churn but excludes additional revenue from add-ons or net expansions (volume/price adjustments). ARR itself represents "the annualized value of active subscription contracts as of the end of each period," with each contract's total value divided by the number of days in the contract term and multiplied by 365, excluding certain short-term or non-core contracts (e.g., terms under one year that are distinct from Workday's core product offering).

answer: Shift4 discloses a concentration risk in that its merchant processing activity in North America is facilitated by a single vendor. Because a majority of the company's revenue is derived from card transaction processing, and Shift4 is not itself a "member bank," it relies on a sponsorship agreement with a member bank to process bank card transactions; if that agreement were breached, Shift4 would have only 180 days to find an alternative bank sponsor. The company states it believes the processing vendor maintains appropriate backup systems and alternative arrangements to avoid significant disruption, but the disclosure highlights the risk of dependence on this single vendor/sponsor relationship for its North American processing.
provenance: Primary 10-K document, Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, "Concentration Risk" section (offset ~393,862 in extracted text), FY2024 10-K (period ended Dec 31, 2024).

answer: Yes — Workday discloses a "Gross Revenue Retention Rate" (approximately 98% as of January 31, 2025) in its FY2025 10-K. It is defined as the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers, calculated by comparing total Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) for a cohort of customers at the prior period-end to ARR from that same customer set at the current period-end. It reflects revenue lost to churn/downgrades but excludes any revenue gained from upsells, add-ons, or net expansion (volume/price increases). No separate "net revenue retention" metric is disclosed.

So Zillow's acquisition capital has been directed at reinforcing and monetizing its still-dominant Residential/For-Sale revenue base, while the shift toward Rentals in the revenue mix has come from organic growth, not M&A.

answer: Essentially all of it. answer: In its FY2024 10-K, Shift4 discloses that its North American merchant processing activity is facilitated by a single (one) vendor, creating a concentration risk. The company states it believes this vendor maintains appropriate backup systems and alternative arrangements to avoid significant processing disruption if an unforeseen event occurs. This reliance is compounded by the fact that a majority of Shift4's revenue derives from card transaction processing, and because Shift4 is not a "member bank" in North America, it must maintain a sponsorship agreement with a member bank; a breach of that agreement could let the sponsor bank terminate it, leaving the company only 180 days to find an alternative bank sponsor.

A majority of the Company's revenue is derived from the processing of card transactions... the Company would have 180 days to identify an alternative bank sponsor."

answer: Allstate's Junior Subordinated Debentures outstanding as of Dec 31, 2024 total $500 million principal — the Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures. Interest is fixed at 6.500%, paid semi-annually, until May 15, 2037; thereafter it floats quarterly at three-month LIBOR (now CME Term SOFR) plus 2.120% (plus a 0.26161% spread adjustment for the SOFR transition). Scheduled maturity is May 15, 2057, with a final legal maturity of May 15, 2067. The debentures are redeemable at par (plus accrued interest) on/after May 15, 2037, or earlier under certain circumstances at par or a make-whole price. Allstate may defer interest for up to 10 consecutive years (compounding), during which it is restricted from paying common/preferred dividends and may be required to raise cash via issuing common stock (75 million shares reserved). The debentures are also subject to a Replacement Capital Covenant restricting early repayment/redemption absent proceeds from qualifying equity issuances, for the benefit of holders of the $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2053 (not the Junior Subordinated Debenture holders), terminating in 2067 (or earlier under specified triggers).

Redeemable in whole/part on or after May 15, 2037 at par plus accrued interest (or earlier, in limited circumstances, at par or a make-whole price). Allstate may defer interest for up to 10 consecutive years (compounding), during which common/preferred dividends are barred; 75 million shares are reserved to potentially satisfy deferred-interest obligations via stock issuance. The debentures are also subject to a Replacement Capital Covenant restricting early repayment/redemption absent qualifying equity proceeds, for the benefit of holders of designated "covered debt" (currently the $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2053), terminating in 2067 (with earlier termination triggers).

answer: Over 2023–2024, Zillow made three acquisitions — all completed in 2023 (Aryeo, ~$35M, July 2023; Spruce, ~$19M, Sept 2023; Follow Up Boss, up to $499M total including contingent consideration, Dec 2023) — with no new acquisitions disclosed for calendar 2024. All three were small, software/technology "tuck-in" deals (CRM, listing-media, and title/escrow platforms) explicitly aimed at building "a more integrated software experience" for real estate professionals, rather than large-scale market-expanding M&A. This aligns with Zillow's revenue mix shift toward transaction-adjacent services: total revenue grew 15.0% in FY2024 (to $2,236M from $1,945M in FY2023), but Mortgages revenue grew 51.0% (to $145M) and Rentals grew 26.9% (to $453M), both outpacing Residential's 9.8% growth (to $1,594M) — so Residential's share of total revenue fell from ~74.7% to ~71.3% while Mortgages and Rentals gained share, consistent with the integration thesis behind the Spruce (title/escrow) and Follow Up Boss/Aryeo (agent software) deals.

This strategy aligns with growth in For Sale revenue (Residential + Mortgages), up 12.3% from $1,548M (2023) to $1,739M (2024), while Mortgages nearly doubled its share (4.9%→6.5%). However, Rentals — not targeted by any of these acquisitions — grew fastest (+26.9%, $357M→$453M) and gained the most revenue-mix share (18.4%→20.3%), so the acquisition strategy tracks the For Sale/transaction ecosystem even as Rentals organically becomes a larger part of the mix.

answer: As of December 31, 2024, Allstate had $500 million outstanding of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures, with a scheduled maturity of May 15, 2057 and final maturity of May 15, 2067. They pay a fixed 6.500% rate semi-annually through May 15, 2037, then convert to a quarterly floating rate of three-month LIBOR (now CME Term SOFR) plus 2.120% plus a 0.26161% spread adjustment. They are redeemable at par plus accrued interest on/after May 15, 2037 (or earlier under certain circumstances, at par or a make-whole price). Allstate may defer interest for up to 10 consecutive years (compounding), during which dividends/buybacks on common/preferred stock are restricted, and if funds cannot otherwise be raised the Company may be required to issue common stock (75 million shares reserved). The debentures are also subject to a Replacement Capital Covenant restricting early repayment/redemption absent proceeds from qualifying equity issuances, for the benefit of holders of the $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2053, with certain exceptions (e.g., an S&P credit rating upgrade to A or above, or a tax-event redemption).

answer: KKR issued 51,750,000 shares of 6.25% Series D Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock on March 7, 2025, for an aggregate liquidation preference of $2.59 billion (net proceeds ~$2.5 billion after issuance costs). Liquidation preference is $50.00/share plus accrued unpaid dividends. Dividends accrue cumulatively at 6.25% annually on the $50.00 liquidation preference, payable quarterly (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec 1) beginning June 1, 2025, in cash, common stock, or a combination, with a stopper on junior-stock dividends/repurchases until Series D dividends are current. Each share mandatorily converts around March 1, 2028 into between 0.3312 and 0.4140 shares of KKR common stock, based on the 20-day VWAP ending just before that date, subject to anti-dilution adjustments. The 10-Q does not disclose specific voting rights for Series D holders or a specific stated use of proceeds beyond reporting it as a Q1 2025 financing-activity cash inflow.

answer: Paylocity's FY2024 10-K (Item 1A, "Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Matters") describes five main regulatory risk categories: (1) general risk that changing regulatory requirements (tax, benefit, wage-and-hour, employment, and other domestic/international laws) could force costly product changes or block new offerings; (2) money transmitter/money services business regulation risk — new statutes or regulatory reinterpretation could require licensing/registration or limit how client payroll funds are handled/invested, with potential civil/criminal fines if found to be operating unlicensed; (3) AI/machine-learning regulatory risk — evolving and expanding U.S./EU/other legislative scrutiny of AI could bring fines, investigations, reputational harm, and litigation (IP, privacy, employment, civil rights) tied to AI use in its products; (4) data privacy law risk — compliance obligations under HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA and other state/international privacy laws, which are non-uniform and rapidly evolving and carry steep penalties (GDPR fines up to 4% of worldwide revenue), with enforcement actions/investigations able to bring penalties and reputational harm; and (5) tax law risk — new, amended, or retroactively applied federal/state/local tax laws (income, sales, use) targeting electronically delivered services, plus varying state sales/use tax rules that could create back-tax, interest, and penalty exposure. The filing states this list is not exhaustive.

These targets reinforce Zillow's existing "For Sale" (Premier Agent/Residential, 71-78% of FY2024's $2,236M total revenue) and mortgage-adjacent businesses: Follow Up Boss/Aryeo/Virtual Staging AI strengthen agent-facing software that the company credits with lifting Residential revenue, while Spruce extends into title/escrow next to Mortgages, the fastest-growing segment (+51% YoY, share up from 5% to 6% of revenue). Rentals, the second-fastest-growing segment (+27% YoY, 18%→20% of revenue), grew organically without a matching acquisition in this window — so acquisition spend was concentrated where it reinforces, rather than diversifies, the evolving revenue mix.

answer: As of Dec 31, 2024, Allstate had $500 million outstanding of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures, with a scheduled maturity of May 15, 2057 and final maturity of May 15, 2067. They pay a fixed 6.500% rate semi-annually through May 15, 2037, then convert to a floating rate of three-month LIBOR (now three-month CME Term SOFR) + 2.120% + a 0.26161% spread adjustment, payable quarterly. They are redeemable at par plus accrued interest on/after May 15, 2037 (or earlier at par plus accrued interest or a make-whole price in certain circumstances), carry a deferral feature allowing Allstate to defer interest up to 10 consecutive years (with compounding, and a common-stock-issuance backstop using 75 million reserved shares), and while interest is deferred, Allstate cannot pay dividends on or redeem common/preferred stock.

answer: Yes. Workday discloses a "Gross Revenue Retention Rate" (approximately 98% as of January 31, 2025) in its FY2025 10-K MD&A. It is defined as the percentage of recurring revenue (based on ARR) retained from existing customers, calculated by comparing total ARR of a customer cohort at the prior period-end to ARR from that same cohort at the current period-end. It captures revenue lost to churn but excludes upsell/cross-sell/expansion revenue (i.e., it is a gross, not net, retention measure). Workday does not separately disclose a "net" revenue retention rate.

answer: Zillow's acquisitions were concentrated in 2023, not 2024: Aryeo (Jul 2023, ~$35M, real-estate photography software), Spruce (Sep 2023, ~$19M, title/escrow platform), and Follow Up Boss (Dec 2023, ~$399M cash + up to $100M contingent consideration, real-estate CRM). No new acquisitions were reported as closing in 2024 (goodwill was flat: $2,823M at 12/31/2024 vs $2,817M at 12/31/2023). These deals were all "bolt-on" software/tooling purchases aimed at deepening the integrated transaction ("housing super app") experience within Zillow's largest segment, For Sale/Residential (71% of FY2024's $2,236M total revenue, up from 75% of FY2023's $1,945M). Management directly credits part of FY2024's 10% Residential revenue growth to the inclusion of Follow Up Boss revenue. Meanwhile, the fastest-growing pieces of the revenue mix — Mortgages (+51% to $145M) and Rentals (+27% to $453M, now 20% of revenue vs 18% in 2023) — grew organically rather than via acquisition. So the acquisition strategy reinforced/monetized the core, slower-growing For Sale/Residential business (adding CRM, marketing, and title/escrow tools for agents and sellers), while the shift in revenue mix toward Mortgages and Rentals came from internal investment (Zillow Home Loans expansion, Rentals traffic/monetization gains) rather than M&A.

answer: Allstate had $500 million of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures outstanding as of Dec 31, 2024. Scheduled maturity May 15, 2057, final maturity May 15, 2067. Interest is 6.500% fixed, paid semi-annually, until May 15, 2037, then floating at three-month LIBOR (now CME Term SOFR) plus 2.120% (plus 0.26161% spread adjustment), paid quarterly. Redeemable in whole/part on/after May 15, 2037 at par plus accrued interest; redeemable earlier only in limited circumstances (e.g., tax event) at par (or make-whole if greater). Allstate may defer interest for up to 10 consecutive years (compounding), during which it cannot pay common/preferred dividends or buy back stock (with limited exceptions), and has reserved 75 million common shares to fund deferred interest if needed. The debentures are also subject to a Replacement Capital Covenant restricting early repayment/redemption absent proceeds from qualifying equity issuances, for the benefit of another series of Allstate debt (currently the $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2053).
provenance: Allstate FY2024 10-K, Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 14 "Capital Structure" — "Junior Subordinated Debentures" subsection (primary document text, offsets ~562,687–569,000).

Interest is fixed at 6.500% paid semi-annually until May 15, 2037, then floats quarterly at 3-month CME Term SOFR + 2.120% + 0.26161% spread adjustment (originally 3-month LIBOR-based). answer: Yes — Workday discloses a Gross Revenue Retention Rate (approximately 98% as of January 31, 2025) in its FY2025 10-K; it does not disclose a separate net retention rate. Definition: it measures the percentage of recurring revenue (based on Annual Recurring Revenue, "ARR") retained from the same set of existing customers between the prior period-end and the current period-end, capturing revenue lost to churn/downgrades but excluding any additional revenue from add-ons, upsells, or net expansions (volume/price increases). answer: Over FY2023–FY2024, Zillow made three acquisitions — all completed in 2023, with none in 2024: Aryeo (real-estate photography/listing software, ~$35M, July 2023), Spruce (title & escrow platform, ~$19-24M, Sept 2023), and Follow Up Boss (real-estate CRM, $484M total consideration including up to $100M contingent, Dec 2023). All were software/technology tuck-ins meant to build a more "integrated software experience"/"housing super app" for agents, lenders and consumers in Zillow's "Enhanced Markets," rather than acquisitions of new revenue streams. This aligns with the revenue mix as of FY2024 (total revenue $2,236M, up from $1,945M in FY2023 and $1,958M in FY2022): Residential revenue ($1,594M, 71% of total revenue) and Mortgages revenue ($145M, up 51% from $96M in FY2023) remain the dominant, acquisition-reinforced "For Sale" categories, while Rentals revenue (the fastest-growing category, $453M in FY2024 vs. $274M in FY2022, +65%) grew organically without any acquisitions. In short, Zillow's 2023 M&A targeted deepening its core Residential/Mortgages transaction ecosystem through software tools (CRM, listing media, title/escrow), while 2024 saw no new deals — consistent with a "housing super app" strategy of integrating the existing For-Sale transaction funnel rather than diversifying revenue via acquisition, even as Rentals organically became a larger share of the mix.

answer: Over FY2023–FY2024 Zillow made a series of small, technology-focused "tuck-in" acquisitions rather than revenue-line acquisitions: Aryeo (7/2023, ~$35M, listing/photography software), Spruce (9/2023, ~$19M, title & escrow platform), Follow Up Boss (12/2023, $399M cash + up to $100M contingent consideration, CRM/lead-management for agents), and Virtual Staging AI (10/2024, AI virtual staging) — continuing a pattern begun with VRX Media Group in 12/2022. Management states these deals are meant to build "a more integrated software experience" supporting its "Enhanced Markets"/"housing super app" strategy (by 12/31/2024, >80% of Enhanced Market connections ran through Follow Up Boss), i.e., they deepen and monetize the existing Residential/For-Sale transaction funnel rather than create new revenue segments. This matches the revenue mix: FY2024 total revenue was $2,236M (Residential $1,594M/71%, Mortgages $145M/6%, For Sale total $1,739M/78%, Rentals $453M/20%, Other $44M/2%) versus FY2023 total $1,945M (Residential $1,452M/75%, Mortgages $96M/5%, For Sale $1,548M/80%, Rentals $357M/18%, Other $40M/2%). While acquisitions targeted software/technology to strengthen the Residential/For-Sale core, the fastest organic growth—and the shift in mix away from Residential's dominance—came from Mortgages (+51% YoY) and Rentals (+27% YoY), which together pulled Residential's share of revenue down from 75% to 71% even as total revenue grew 15%. So acquisitions have reinforced (rather than diversified) the core transaction ecosystem, while the revenue mix is organically diversifying toward Mortgages and Rentals.
